data: Is the size of the KIC-tree consistently lower than the size of the graph for all values of vertices and keywords?

The question asks whether the size of the KIC-tree is consistently lower than the size of the graph for all values of vertices and keywords. From the caption, we know that the figure shows the index size for varying vertices and keywords. The two lines represent the graph size and the KIC-tree size.

Looking at the left graph, which shows the relationship between the number of vertices and the size of the graph and KIC-tree, we can see that the KIC-tree size line (purple) is consistently below the graph size line (cyan) across all values of vertices. This indicates that the KIC-tree size is lower than the graph size for all values of vertices.

Similarly, looking at the right graph, which shows the relationship between the number of keywords and the size of the graph and KIC-tree, we can see that the KIC-tree size line (purple) is consistently below the graph size line (cyan) across all values of keywords. This also indicates that the KIC-tree size is lower than the graph size for all values of keywords.

Therefore, based on the analysis of both graphs, the size of the KIC-tree is consistently lower than the size of the graph for all values of vertices and keywords.
